Judgement:
The appellant is 2nd respondent/Insurance company and the respondents are claim petitioner and

sentences.text: The appellant filed the appeal questioning the legal validity of the order of the Tribunal.
2. Both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in the claim application.

3. The claim petitioner filed the petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road accident which took place on 07.02.2004 on Rajampeta-Kodur main road near Mukkavaripalli Village.
4. The brief averments in the petition filed by the petitioner are as follows:
VGKR ,

J On 02.02.2004 the petitioner and others were engaged in a lorry bearing registration No.HR 46C 7177 belonged to the 1st respondent for loading of Papaya fruits and when the lorry reached near Mukkavaripalli Village on Rajampet-Kodur road, the driver of the lorry drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, due to which, the lorry turned turtle and all the coolies including the petitioner sustained injuries and the petitioner was admitted to SVRRGG Hospital, Tirupati for treatment.

The 1st respondent is owner and the 2nd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle and hence, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
5.
The 1st respondent remained set ex parte.
The 2nd respondent/Insurance company filed a counter by denying the manner of accident, nature of injuries allegedly sustained by the petitioner and the treatment and the expenditure incurred by him.

6. Based on the above pleadings of both the parties, the following issues were settled for trial by the Tribunal:
1) Whether the driver of the lorry bearing No.HR 46C 7177 drove the same in rash and negligent manner and caused the VGKR,J accident on 07.02.2004 and as a result, the petitioner sustained injuries?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount?

sentences.text: During the course of enquiry, on behalf of the petitioner, P.Ws.1 to 4 were examined and got marked Exs.A.1 to A.5 and Ex
.X.1-case sheet was marked through P.W.4.

On behalf of the 2nd respondent/Insurance company, R.W.1 was examined and got marked Ex.B.1.
8.

Basing on the material available on record, the Tribunal came to a conclusion that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the crime vehicle and accordingly,
granted an amount of Rs.1,81,680/- with interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit against the respondents.
Aggrieved against the said order, the appellant/Insurance company preferred the present appeal.
9. Heard arguments of learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for the 1st respondent/claim petitioner.
VGKR,J 10.

The appellant pleaded that the Tribunal erred in fastening the liability on the appellant and that the petitioner was an unauthorized passenger in the crime vehicle and his risk is not covered by Ex.B.1- policy.

11. Now, the point for determination is:
Whether the order of the Tribunal needs any interference of this Court?
12. POINT:

The evidence of P.Ws.1 and 2 coupled with Ex.A.1- certified copy of first information report and Ex.A.2-certified copy of charge sheet clearly proves that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the crime vehicle.
The Tribunal also gave the same finding.
Therefore, there is no need to interfere with the said finding given by the Tribunal.
13. The claim petitioner is the injured in this case.
As per Ex.A.3- certified copy of wound certificate and as per the evidence of P.Ws.3 and 4, the petitioner sustained three injuries.
P.W.4, who is an Orthopedic Surgeon, SVRRGG Hospital, Tirupati, deposed that VGKR,J he had not treated the petitioner, but the petitioner was attended by Doctor Hari Babu.

At the time of giving evidence,
P.W.4 brought the case sheet of the petitioner and the same was marked as Ex.X.1.
As per the evidence of P.W.4, the petitioner sustained three injuries, from out of which, injuries 2 and 3 are grievous in nature.
As per Ex.X.1-case sheet, the patient was admitted on 07.02.2004 and discharged on 14.02.2004.
The material on record proves that injuries 2 and 3 are grievous in nature and injury No.1 is simple in nature.
As can be seen from Ex.A.3-wound certificate, it is evident that there are fractures in 2nd to 6th ribs on the left side and there is a fracture in lower 1/3rd of right tibia.
Thus, there are six fractures.
14. The petitioner claims that because of the accident, he sustained disability of 35%.
P.W.3 deposed that he examined the petitioner on 12.08.2011 before the District Medical Board, RIMS, Kadapa.

2 further deposed that he assessed the disability of the petitioner at 35%.
On considering the entire material on record, the Tribunal came to conclusion that the disability of the petitioner is 20% only.
VGKR,J 15.
As per the case of the petitioner, he is a coolie in loading and unloading.
But, the petitioner did not adduce any evidence to prove his earnings.
However, the Tribunal took his monthly earnings as Rs.2,100/-.
The same is not challenged by the petitioner.
The age of the petitioner is said to be 28 years at the time of accident.
The material on record also reveals the same.
Hence, the Tribunal took the age of the petitioner as 28 years at the time of accident.

16. By applying the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Sarla Varma case, the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.85,680/- (Rs.2,100/- x 20/100 x 12 x 17) towards permanent disability of 20% sustained by the petitioner.

The Tribunal also awarded an amount of Rs.90,000/-
towards fracture injuries and Rs.1,000/- towards one simple injury.
Thus, in all, the petitioner is entitled compensation of Rs.1,81,680/-.
There is no need to interfere with the said finding given by the Tribunal.

17. The contention of the 2nd respondent/Insurance company is that the petitioner was travelling in the 1st respondent's lorry which is a goods carrying vehicle at the time of accident, and that the VGKR,J petitioner is an unauthorized passenger.
As per the case of the petitioner, he and others were travelling in the crime vehicle for loading and unloading purpose and they were engaged by the 1st respondent for the said purpose.
It is not disputed by both sides that the 1st respondent's vehicle was insured as a goods carrying commercial vehicle.
As per the material on record, the petitioner was travelling in the offending vehicle as a coolie for loading and unloading of papaya fruits.
Therefore, the petitioner is not a gratuitous passenger.
As per Ex.B.1-copy of Insurance policy
, the policy covers insurance for four persons for loading and unloading of goods.
The evidence on record clearly proves that the driver of the crime vehicle was having a valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
Therefore, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
18. In view of the above observations, there are no merits in the appeal and the appeal is devoid of merits and it is liable to be dismissed.
19. In the result, the appeal is dismissed.
No order as to costs.

VGKR,J Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this appeal shall stand closed.
_______________________________ V.GOPALA KRISHNA RAO, J th 19 April, 2023 cbs
VGKR,J HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE V.GOPALA KRISHNA RAO 19th April, 2023 cbs The National Insurance Co Ltd vs Chodavaram Siva Nagaiah
